claims.text: Equiatomic FeCoNi has an fcc crystal structure.
Equiatomic FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
Equiatomic FeCoNi has a low coercive field and soft-ferromagnetic behavior.
Gas nitriding FeCoNi in NH3 at 400–500°C will introduce interstitial nitrogen.
The incorporated nitrogen will occupy octahedral interstitial sites.
Interstitial nitrogen will induce a slight tetragonal distortion of the fcc lattice.
Nitrogen-induced lattice distortion will lower the crystal symmetry.
The lowered symmetry and lattice distortion will enhance magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Interstitial nitrogen and its associated distortions will create or strengthen domain-wall pinning sites.
Enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy and domain-wall pinning will increase coercivity.
Controlled nitriding will produce higher coercivity than untreated equiatomic FeCoNi.
Controlled nitriding will cause only a minimal reduction in saturation magnetization if nitride precipitation is prevented.
Precisely controlling nitriding pressure and duration can avoid excessive nitrogen uptake and nitride precipitation.
The intervention can apply to both bulk samples and thin films when the equiatomic high-entropy phase is preserved.
Aggressive nitriding can cause nitride precipitation or major phase separation.
The coercivity response is sensitive to nitriding parameters and to the nitrogen-incorporation threshold for deleterious phase formation.

contradictions.description: Nitride precipitation is defined as outside the hypothesis's effective regime, but it is also treated as a result that falsifies the hypothesis. A sample processed outside the stated regime would ordinarily test failure to satisfy the boundary conditions rather than decisively falsify the within-regime prediction.
